related_questions.question: What features are required for a primary stroke center?

text_blocks.snippet: A primary stroke center (PSC) is distinguished by its ability to provide prompt and effective treatment for acute ischemic stroke, including the administration of intravenous thrombolytics (like tPA). Key features include a dedicated stroke team, advanced diagnostic imaging, and the ability to manage and stabilize patients before potentially transferring more complex cases to a comprehensive stroke center.
snippet_highlighted_words: a dedicated stroke team, advanced diagnostic imaging, and the ability to manage and stabilize patients before potentially transferring more complex cases to a comprehensive stroke center

list.title: Rapid Assessment and Treatment:
list.snippet: PSCs are equipped to quickly assess stroke patients, perform necessary imaging (like CT scans), and administer tPA to eligible patients within the critical time window.

list.title: Dedicated Stroke Team:
list.snippet: A PSC has a team of qualified medical professionals specifically trained in stroke care, ensuring efficient and coordinated care.

list.title: Advanced Imaging Capabilities:
list.snippet: PSCs can perform advanced imaging, such as CT and MRI, to help diagnose the type and location of the stroke.

list.title: Transfer Protocols:
list.snippet: While PSCs can manage many stroke cases, they have established protocols for transferring patients with severe or complex strokes to comprehensive stroke centers for specialized care or procedures.

list.title: Stroke Unit or Beds:
list.snippet: A dedicated stroke unit or specific beds for stroke patients are often a requirement for PSC certification.

list.title: Data Collection and Quality Improvement:
list.snippet: PSCs collect data on their stroke treatment performance to continuously improve their care processes and outcomes.

list.title: Telemedicine:
list.snippet: Some PSCs utilize telemedicine to enhance their capabilities, particularly in areas with limited access to specialists.
